body:
👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: The webcam's seek lead is in wall seconds, which matches media time only at 1× (confidence medium)**

Before this PR the preview always ran at 1×. `WebcamLayer` already copies the main element's `playbackRate` onto the webcam `<video>` (`webcam-layer.tsx:113`). But when it resyncs, it seeks ahead by `webcamSeekLead(moving, lastSeekSeconds)` (`webcam-layer.tsx:151`, `webcam-sync.ts:55-58`). `lastSeekSeconds` is the wall time the last seek took (`seekStartedAt` uses `performance.now()`, `webcam-layer.tsx:153`).

At 2× the main video covers twice that much media time during the seek, so the webcam lands about `lastSeekSeconds` behind the screen. At 0.5× it lands ahead by half of that. When that gap is above `WEBCAM_DRIFT_SECONDS` (the same long-keyframe case the lead was added for), the next frame seeks again. That is the "series of seeks" the comment at `webcam-layer.tsx:111-112` warns about.

A possible fix is to multiply the lead by `main.playbackRate`. The file that needs the change is in another part of this review. I'm raising it here because this hook is what now makes rates other than 1× reachable. The PR body also says no real recording at 2× was watched.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Every split that stays contiguous in source now forces a seek during playback (confidence medium)**

`handOffAtCut` calls `advanceFrom(entry.timelineEnd)` whenever `currentTime >= entry.sourceEnd - END_EPSILON`, and it now runs on every rAF frame. `advanceFrom` always calls `seekVideoToSource(next.sourceStart)` for a clip (line 206).

Take a clip split but not deleted. `splitClipAt` (`timeline.ts:93-106`) gives `a = [s, cut]` and `b = [cut, e]`, back to back on the timeline and in source. Playback reaches `cut - 0.02` and the frame loop seeks the `<video>` to `cut`, a position it was about to play anyway.

Before this change, only `onVideoTimeUpdate` checked for the cut, about every 250 ms. A timeupdate past `cut` mapped into `b` through `sourceToTimeline`, so playback continued with no seek. Only a timeupdate landing in the 20 ms window before the cut sought. Now every contiguous boundary seeks, on every pass.

A seek on a `<video>` has to decode again from the previous keyframe. That gives a visible hitch and an audio glitch, and screen recordings can have long GOPs. The user sees and hears a stutter at each split point, where playback used to be seamless. The new tests cover contiguous-in-source only with a slide in between (`CONTIGUOUS_THEN_SLIDE`), never two adjacent clips.

Suggested fix: in `handOffAtCut`, or in `advanceFrom` when it is called from a clip, check for a next entry that is a clip with `next.sourceStart === entry.sourceEnd`. In that case, move `activeClipIdRef` to it and do not seek. Add a test where `seeks` stays empty across `[clip("a",0,5), clip("b",5,10)]`.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · **Still open** at `93a721a`: Still open. `webcam-layer.tsx:151-154` still adds `webcamSeekLead(moving, lastSeekSeconds.current)`, which is measured in wall seconds, and does not scale it by `main.playbackRate`. Nothing in this round changes that path. At 2× or 0.5× the webcam bubble can still land off by the lead and seek again.

<!-- wachi:reply -->

👮 **Wachiman** · **Still open** at `6d2bf6a`: Still open. This round only changed the hook. `webcam-layer.tsx:151` still passes the wall-clock `lastSeekSeconds` to `webcamSeekLead` without scaling it by `main.playbackRate`, while line 113 does copy the rate onto the webcam element.

<!-- wachi:reply -->

👮 **Wachiman** · **Looks addressed** at `6d2bf6a`: Addressed. `handOffAtCut` now checks whether the next layout entry is a clip that starts within END_EPSILON of this clip's `sourceEnd` (lines 263-284). In that case it only moves `activeClipIdRef` on and reports a time that can't go backwards, with no seek. The new tests show `seeks` stays `[]` across `[x 0..5, y 5..10]` at all four speeds, on both the frame path and the timeupdate path.

<!-- wachi:reply -->

👮 **Wachiman** · **Looks addressed** at `9c07227`: Addressed. `webcamSeekLead` now multiplies the wall-time seek duration by the main element's `playbackRate` before it applies the drift threshold and the cap (`webcam-sync.ts:59-63`). `webcam-layer.tsx:151` passes `main?.playbackRate ?? 1`. Unit tests and layer tests cover 2× and 0.5×.

<!-- wachi:reply -->

👮 **Wachiman** · **Looks addressed** at `9c07227`: Addressed. When the next clip continues the same footage (`|next.sourceStart − entry.sourceEnd| < END_EPSILON`), `handOffAtCut` now only moves the bookkeeping on and does not seek (`use-preview-playback.ts:246-269`). Cuts with a gap in source and slides still go through `advanceFrom`.

<!-- wachi:reply -->
